content: This medication may interact with other substances in your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Examples of such substances include mitotane, rifampin, and St. John’s Wort. This medication can reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, which may result in unintended pregnancy. Additionally, it may increase the risk of certain side effects associated with hormonal birth control. It is essential to discuss alternative reliable birth control methods with your doctor and use an effective barrier method, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity to reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. Before starting this medication and while taking it, laboratory and medical tests should be conducted. These tests may include assessments of kidney and liver function, hepatitis B virus testing, viral load measurements, T-cell counts, blood mineral levels, bone density tests, and urine glucose/protein levels. It is crucial to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication in its original container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. If you have hepatitis B infection, stopping this medication may worsen or cause severe symptoms. Consult your doctor before discontinuing this medication. Your doctor will monitor your liver function for several months after stopping elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir. This medication is used to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, allowing your immune system to function more effectively. This decreases the risk of HIV-related complications, such as new infections or cancer, and improves your quality of life. This product contains four medications: elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir. Elvitegravir is an integrase inhibitor, and cobicistat enhances its effectiveness. However, this medication is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as directed by your doctor. Avoid sharing personal items, such as needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors, that may have come into contact with blood or other body fluids. Read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting this medication and each time you get a refill. It is crucial to take this medication exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Take it at least two hours before or after other products that may interfere with its effectiveness. For optimal results, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Do not take more or less of this drug than prescribed, and do not stop taking it without your doctor’s approval. Common side effects may include diarrhea, headache, dizziness, trouble sleeping, unusual dreams, back pain, or changes in the color of the skin on your palms or soles. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off pre-existing infections, potentially causing symptoms to reappear. In rare cases, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Rarely, this medication can cause severe, potentially fatal liver and blood problems, such as lactic acidosis. Tenofovir may increase the risk of bone loss. Discuss the risks and benefits of treatment with your doctor, as well as the potential use of calcium and vitamin D to mitigate this side effect. If you are at risk for bone loss, your doctor may monitor your bone mineral density. A severe allergic reaction to this drug is rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, or tenofovir, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate dizziness. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication is not recommended for use during pregnancy, as it may not work effectively in pregnant women. If you become pregnant or suspect you may be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. Emtricitabine and tenofovir pass into breast milk, but it is unknown if elvitegravir or cobicistat do. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Do not take this medication with other HIV medications, such as ritonavir. This medication can slow the removal of other drugs from your body, potentially affecting their effectiveness. Similarly, other medications can affect the removal of this drug from your body, altering its effectiveness. Examples include mitotane and rifampin. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. It may also increase the risk of certain side effects associated with hormonal birth control. Discuss alternative reliable birth control methods with your doctor and use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity to reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others.
